release.body:
## New

* 82545bb feat: add `managed_updates` to apply builds staged by an updater by @Bush2021

    > I'm also introducing [Pitstop](https://github.com/Bush2021/pitstop), my new Windows app for configuring Chrome++ Next and managing portable Chrome. It provides a graphical settings editor, updates for Chrome and Chrome++ Next, version rollback, and portable-profile backups before major Chrome updates.

    > Chrome++ 1.19.0 adds the integration Pitstop needs for background and in-app updates. Pitstop prepares the new build, and Chrome's "Relaunch to update" applies it. Pitstop enables `managed_updates` automatically, so no manual INI edit is needed.

## Fix

* 0d80d13 fix: run launch commands once, without a console window by @Bush2021

    > Opening a link from another app no longer reruns `launch_on_startup` or triggers `launch_on_exit` in the process that forwards the link to the running browser.

    > Commands in `launch_on_startup` and `launch_on_exit` now run without a console window by default. If a command needs a console or interactive input, change it to `start "" <command>`. Programs with their own windows still display them normally.

* 84d01b5 fix: run exit commands before a relaunched browser's startup commands by @Bush2021

    > On relaunch, Chrome now waits up to 3 seconds for `launch_on_exit` commands before the new browser runs `launch_on_startup`. This gives cleanup commands time to finish before helper programs restart. Startup commands proceed after the wait even if an exit command is still running.

* 7b80a11 fix: match launch switches by argument, not by substring by @Bush2021

    > Links containing text such as `content-type=` or `--portable` no longer get mistaken for launch switches. Opening these links from another app now preserves the configured portable profile instead of potentially opening Chrome with the default profile.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Bush2021/chrome_plus/compare/1.18.3...1.19.0
